name: Willy Planckaert
milestone_by_age_26: Won the silver medal in the amateur road race at the 1964 UCI World Championships in Sallanches at age 20, and won the points classification plus two stages at the 1966 Tour de France at age 22.
early_history_summary: Planckaert was born into a Belgian cycling family in Nevele; his brothers Eddy and Walter also became professional cyclists. He won the silver medal at the 1964 World Championships as an amateur, then turned professional and immediately won stages and the points classification at the 1966 Tour de France.
family_context_summary: Born into a cycling family in Nevele, Belgium; brothers Eddy and Walter Planckaert also became professional road cyclists, and son Jo Planckaert raced professionally as well.
parent_family_domain_summary: The Planckaert family is a Belgian cycling dynasty with multiple brothers and a son who all became professional cyclists, indicating deep family-domain immersion in the sport.
primary_early_advantage_tags: cycling dynasty,belgian cycling culture,sibling rivalry,early pro exposure
evidence_summary: Planckaert came from a deep Belgian cycling dynasty with three brothers and a son all racing professionally. Belgium's Flanders region was a global epicenter of cycling culture, providing immersion and infrastructure. He won silver at the 1964 World Championships as an amateur at 20 and the Tour de France points classification at 22, demonstrating early competitive maturity likely built on years of family-influenced training.
starting_point: Born into a working-class Belgian cycling family in Nevele, Flanders; multiple brothers became professional cyclists, creating a family-domain immersion in the sport from childhood.
current_position: Retired former professional road cyclist; last known to be living in Belgium as of 2025.

trajectory.event: Won silver medal in the amateur road race at the UCI World Championships in Sallanches, France.
Won the points classification and two stages at the Tour de France in his breakout professional season.
Won three stages at the Giro d'Italia, demonstrating versatility across grand tours.
Won overall at the Étoile de Bessèges, one of his later career victories before retirement.

name: David Ho
milestone_by_age_26: No material professional milestone by age 26 found; Ho earned his MD from Harvard Medical School in 1978 at age 26, but this is an educational credential rather than a professional achievement. His pioneering HIV/AIDS research began in the 1980s and his breakthrough combination therapy work came in 1996 at age 44.
early_history_summary: Ho immigrated from Taiwan to the US in 1965 at age 12, grew up in Los Angeles, and graduated from Caltech with a BS in biology with highest honors in 1974. He earned his MD from Harvard Medical School in 1978, then completed clinical training at UCLA and Massachusetts General Hospital before beginning his research career.
family_context_summary: Born in Taichung, Taiwan to a modest family; father was an electrical engineer who moved to the US in 1957 as a graduate student. The family lived in a modest four-room house in Taiwan before reuniting in California.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Ho Pu-chi graduated from Zhejiang University and earned a degree in electrical engineering from USC, providing an educational role model but not direct domain expertise in medicine or virology.
evidence_summary: Ho's MD from Harvard in 1978 at age 26 is an impressive educational credential but not a material professional milestone in the sense of an independently verifiable achievement in his field. His pioneering HIV/AIDS combination therapy research, which earned him Time Person of the Year in 1996, came 18 years later. No dated material professional milestone by age 26 is documented.

name: Ernesto Hoost
milestone_by_age_26: Won the WMTA Muay Thai World Championship and Savate World Championship in 1989 at age 24, and the WKA World Kickboxing Championship and WMTA Muay Thai World Championship in 1990 at age 25, establishing himself as a multi-discipline world champion before 26.
early_history_summary: Hoost was born in Heemskerk, Netherlands to Surinamese parents and played football until age 15, when he began training in kickboxing at the newly opened Sokudo Gym. He had his first match in 1983 at age 18, winning by knockout. From 1988 his career accelerated as he won multiple European and world titles in Savate and Muay Thai under trainer Johan Vos at Vos Gym.
family_context_summary: Born to Surinamese parents in Heemskerk, Netherlands; family financial background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: dutch kickboxing ecosystem,vos gym,johan vos trainer,early competition
evidence_summary: Hoost benefited from the Netherlands' position as a global epicenter of kickboxing and Muay Thai, with access to legendary trainers like Johan Vos at Vos Gym. He started training at 15 and competing at 18, building years of reps before winning world titles at 24-25. The Dutch kickboxing ecosystem of the 1980s, with gyms producing multiple world champions, provided a frontier-level training environment that accelerated his development.
starting_point: Born to Surinamese parents in Heemskerk, Netherlands; family background and financial status not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Retired from professional kickboxing in 2006; runs training and makes occasional appearances; widely regarded as one of the greatest kickboxers of all time with four K-1 World Grand Prix titles.

trajectory.event: Won his first kickboxing match by knockout in the second round at Sokudo Gym.
Won the WMTA Muay Thai World Championship and the Savate World Championship, establishing himself as a multi-discipline world title holder.
Won the WKA World Kickboxing Championship and a second WMTA Muay Thai World Championship.
Reached the final of the inaugural K-1 World Grand Prix, losing to Branko Cikatic; won the K-2 World Championship later that year.
Won his first K-1 World Grand Prix championship, defeating Andy Hug by unanimous decision.
Won his fourth K-1 World Grand Prix title, cementing his legacy as one of the all-time greats.

name: Michael J. Fox
milestone_by_age_26: Cast as Alex P. Keaton on the NBC sitcom Family Ties in 1982 at age 21, which became a hit show with his character as the focal point; won three consecutive Emmy Awards for the role in 1986-1988 and starred in Back to the Future (1985) at age 24, becoming a global teen idol and box-office star by 26.
early_history_summary: Fox began acting as a child in Canada, starring in the CBC series Leo and Me at age 16. He moved to Los Angeles in 1979 at age 18 and landed early film roles in Midnight Madness (1980) and Class of 1984 (1982). His breakthrough came when he was cast as Alex P. Keaton on Family Ties in 1982, which quickly made his character the show's focus. He then starred in Back to the Future (1985), which spent eight consecutive weekends as the number-one US box office film.
family_context_summary: Born in Edmonton, Alberta to a military family; father William Fox served 25 years in the Royal Canadian Corps of Signals and later worked as a police dispatcher; mother Phyllis was a payroll clerk and actress. The family lived in various Canadian cities before settling in Burnaby, BC in 1971.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early start in canada,move to LA,sitcom casting,teen idol wave
evidence_summary: Fox started acting at 15 in Canadian television and moved to LA at 18 to pursue acting full-time, accumulating several years of reps before his breakthrough. His casting on Family Ties in 1982 at age 21 was pivotal; the show's structure shifted to center on his character, and he won three consecutive Emmys (1986-88). Back to the Future (1985) made him a global box-office star at 24. He rode the 1980s teen entertainment wave with strong comedic timing and work ethic, famously shooting Family Ties and Back to the Future simultaneously.
starting_point: Born into a middle-class Canadian military family in Edmonton, Alberta; father was a 25-year army veteran turned police dispatcher, mother a payroll clerk; family moved frequently before settling in Burnaby, BC.
current_position: Retired from acting in 2020 due to Parkinson's disease progression; founded the Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson's Research in 2000; received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2025.

trajectory.event: Starred in the Canadian CBC television series Leo and Me, his first significant acting role.
Cast as Alex P. Keaton on NBC's Family Ties, which became a hit sitcom centered on his character.
Starred as Marty McFly in Back to the Future, which spent eight consecutive weekends as the number-one US box office film and grossed $381 million worldwide.
Won his first Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Comedy Series for Family Ties, becoming the youngest actor ever to win the prize.
Won his third consecutive Emmy for Family Ties and married Tracy Pollan.
Diagnosed with Parkinson's disease, which he publicly disclosed in 1998.
Founded the Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson's Research, which became the largest nonprofit funder of Parkinson's research.
Received the Presidential Medal of Freedom from President Biden.

name: Claude Makélélé
milestone_by_age_26: Won the French Ligue 1 championship with Nantes in the 1994-95 season at age 22, and helped Nantes reach the UEFA Champions League semi-final the following season, earning a move to Marseille and then Celta Vigo by age 25.
early_history_summary: Makélélé was born in Kinshasa, Zaire and moved to a Paris suburb at age 4. His father was a footballer who played for DR Congo. He signed for Sporting Melun-Dammarie at 15, joined Brest's training centre at 16, and was recruited by Nantes in December 1991 at age 18. He broke into Nantes' first team in the 1992-93 season and became a key player, winning the 1995 French title.
family_context_summary: Born in Kinshasa, Zaire (now DRC) to a footballer father who played for DR Congo and ended his career in Belgium's third division; family moved to a Paris suburb in 1977 when Makélélé was 4.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father André-Joseph Makélélé was a professional footballer who represented DR Congo and played in Belgium's third division, providing direct domain exposure and footballing knowledge from birth.
primary_early_advantage_tags: nantes academy,father footballer,french football pipeline,early pro contract
evidence_summary: Makélélé benefited from his father's professional football background and France's elite youth development pipeline. He entered Nantes' professional system at 18, a club renowned for developing talent under coach Jean Claude Suaudeau. The Nantes system honed his positional intelligence and work rate, leading to a Ligue 1 title at 22 and a Champions League semi-final run. His father's footballing career provided early domain exposure, and the French football ecosystem offered a clear pathway from youth to professional.
starting_point: Born in Kinshasa, Zaire to a professional footballer father who played for DR Congo; family immigrated to a Paris suburb at age 4, providing access to France's youth football development system.
current_position: Former football manager; last managed Asteras Tripolis in Greece in 2024; widely regarded as one of the greatest defensive midfielders of all time, with the position sometimes called the 'Makélélé Role.'

trajectory.event: Signed a professional contract with Nantes after being recruited from Brest's training centre.
Won the French Ligue 1 championship with Nantes, the club's first title in 12 years.
Helped Nantes reach the UEFA Champions League semi-final, losing to Juventus 4-3 on aggregate.
Moved to Celta Vigo in La Liga, beginning his rise to global prominence.
Signed for Real Madrid, joining the Galácticos and winning the 2001-02 UEFA Champions League.
Signed for Chelsea, where he redefined the defensive midfield role and won two Premier League titles.
Reached the FIFA World Cup final with France, losing to Italy on penalties.

name: Gulshan Kumar
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Kumar founded Super Cassettes Industries (T-Series) in 1983 at age 27, and his major Bollywood breakthrough came with Aashiqui in 1990 at age 34. By age 26 (1982), he was running a family cassette shop in Delhi.
early_history_summary: Kumar was born in Delhi to a Punjabi Hindu refugee family from West Punjab. His father was a fruit juice vendor in Daryaganj. The family later acquired a shop selling records and inexpensive audio cassettes, which led Kumar to start his own audio cassette operation, Super Cassettes Industries, in 1983. His first Bollywood film was in 1989 and the breakout hit Aashiqui came in 1990.
family_context_summary: Born to a Punjabi Hindu refugee family from Jhang, West Punjab who came to Delhi after the 1947 partition; father was a fruit juice vendor in Daryaganj, Delhi. The family later acquired a shop selling records and cassettes.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; the family's entry into the cassette business appears to have been opportunistic rather than domain-inherited.
evidence_summary: Kumar's years active are listed as 1972-1997, but this likely refers to his early work in the family's fruit juice and cassette shop. He founded Super Cassettes Industries (T-Series) in 1983 at age 27, and his first Bollywood film production was in 1989 at age 33. The breakout hit Aashiqui came in 1990. No material, independently verifiable professional milestone by age 26 is documented.

name: Hugo Gatti
milestone_by_age_26: Made his Primera División debut for Atlanta in 1962 at age 18, was acquired by River Plate in 1964 at age 20 where he played 77 matches over four seasons, and was part of Argentina's 1966 World Cup squad at age 22, with his international debut following in 1967.
early_history_summary: Gatti grew up in Carlos Tejedor, Buenos Aires Province, and was inspired by River Plate goalkeeper Amadeo Carrizo at age 16. He started playing for Atlanta in the Argentine sixth division and made his Primera División debut in 1962 at 18. After 38 matches for Atlanta, he was signed by River Plate in 1964, where he alternated with his idol Carrizo as first-choice goalkeeper for four seasons.
family_context_summary: Born in Carlos Tejedor, Buenos Aires Province; youngest of siblings. Family financial background and parents' occupations not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: argentine football,river plate,amadeo carrizo mentor,early primera division
evidence_summary: Gatti grew up in Argentina, one of the world's premier football nations, and was immersed in the Buenos Aires football ecosystem from his teens. He was inspired by and then directly trained under Amadeo Carrizo at River Plate, one of Argentina's biggest clubs. The Argentine Primera División provided elite-level competition from age 18, and being named to the 1966 World Cup squad at 22 confirmed his early elite status. His innovative goalkeeping style was shaped by the Argentine football culture that valued creativity and flair.
starting_point: Born in Carlos Tejedor, a small town in Buenos Aires Province, Argentina; youngest of siblings; family financial background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Died on 20 April 2025 at age 80 in Buenos Aires after complications from a hip fracture and hospital-acquired infection; final role was as a football media commentator in Spain and Argentina.

trajectory.event: Made his Primera División debut for Atlanta against Gimnasia y Esgrima La Plata.
Signed for River Plate, one of Argentina's biggest clubs, and alternated as first-choice goalkeeper with his idol Amadeo Carrizo.
Named to Argentina's 1966 World Cup squad, though he did not play as backup to Antonio Roma.
Transferred to Gimnasia y Esgrima La Plata, where he played 244 league matches over five seasons.
Joined Boca Juniors, where he became legendary, winning the Metropolitano and Copa Libertadores double in his first year.
Saved a crucial penalty in the Copa Libertadores final against Cruzeiro, helping Boca win the title.
Voted Player of the Year of Argentina.
Played his last professional match on 11 September 1988, retiring at age 44 after 765 league appearances.
Died on 20 April 2025 in Buenos Aires after complications from a hip fracture and hospital-acquired infection.

name: Cindy Kiro
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Kiro was studying social work at Massey University and the University of Auckland in her early twenties. Her first significant professional role was as a senior lecturer at Massey University from 1995 (age ~37), and she became Children's Commissioner in 2003 (age 45).

She joined the first cohort of social work students at Massey University and later graduated with a BA in social sciences from the University of Auckland. She gained a certificate in epidemiology from the European University Institute in 1987.
family_context_summary: Born in Whangārei as the eldest of six children; of Māori (Ngā Puhi, Ngāti Kahu, Ngāti Hine) and English descent. Raised partly by her maternal grandparents, whose surname Kiro she adopted. Grew up in South and West Auckland.
evidence_summary: Kiro's career milestones came later in life: her PhD in 2001 (age ~43), Children's Commissioner role in 2003 (age 45), and Governor-General appointment in 2021 (age 63). By age 26 (~1984), she was completing her university education. No material, independently verifiable professional milestone by age 26 is documented.

name: Egon Zimmermann
milestone_by_age_26: Won gold in giant slalom and bronze in downhill at the 1962 World Championships in Chamonix at age 23, was named European 'Skier of the Year' in 1963, and won Olympic gold in the downhill at the 1964 Innsbruck Winter Olympics at age 25, appearing on the cover of Sports Illustrated.
early_history_summary: Zimmermann was raised on a farm near Lech, Vorarlberg, Austria, which blossomed into a ski resort during his childhood. His family converted their farmhouse into a pension. Despite post-war poverty and having no formal training, he won a clean sweep of the 1958 Junior Championships at age 19 after returning from a forced chef apprenticeship in Paris. He was promoted to the Austrian national team and won World Championship medals at 23.
family_context_summary: Raised on a farm near Lech, Vorarlberg, Austria, during post-World War II poverty. His family converted their farmhouse into a pension as Lech developed into a ski resort. His father forced him into a chef apprenticeship in Paris at 15, interrupting his skiing development.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; the family ran a farm and later a pension in a growing ski resort town, providing geographic proximity to skiing but not direct domain expertise.
primary_early_advantage_tags: lech ski resort,austrian national team,growing up in ski town,post-war adversity
evidence_summary: Zimmermann's key advantage was growing up in Lech am Arlberg as it transformed into a world-class ski resort, providing daily access to the mountains and an emerging alpine skiing culture. Despite post-war poverty and fourth-hand skis, the geographic immersion in Austria's skiing frontier compensated for lack of formal training. His promotion to the national team at 18 gave him access to elite coaching and competition. The adversity of his interrupted development (forced chef apprenticeship) may have created urgency when he returned to skiing.
starting_point: Raised on a farm near Lech, Vorarlberg, Austria during post-WWII poverty; family converted their farmhouse into a pension as Lech developed into a ski resort, providing geographic immersion in alpine skiing culture.
current_position: Died on 23 August 2019 at age 80 in Lech, Austria; had owned a hotel in Lech am Arlberg and suffered from multiple sclerosis in later life.

trajectory.event: Won a clean sweep of the Austrian Junior Championships after returning from a forced chef apprenticeship in Paris.
Won gold in giant slalom and bronze in downhill at the World Championships in Chamonix, France.
Named 'Skier of the Year' by European journalists after an outstanding season with multiple race victories.
Won Olympic gold in the downhill at the Innsbruck Winter Olympics on home soil, appearing on the cover of Sports Illustrated.
Competed at the Grenoble Winter Olympics, finishing 13th in the downhill before retiring from competitive skiing.
Died on 23 August 2019 in Lech, Austria, after suffering from multiple sclerosis.

name: Simen Agdestein
milestone_by_age_26: Became Norwegian national chess champion at age 15 in 1982, earned the International Master title at 16, became a Grandmaster at 18 in 1985, won an individual gold medal at the 1982 Chess Olympiad, and finished second at the 1986 World Junior Championship, all before age 26.
early_history_summary: Agdestein was born in Asker, Norway to a civil engineer father and secretary mother. He became Norwegian national champion at 15, International Master at 16, and Grandmaster at 18. He simultaneously pursued a football career, playing for Lyn Oslo from 1984 and representing Norway's national football team. He won nine Norwegian Chess Championships between 1982 and 2023.
family_context_summary: Born in Asker, Norway as the son of civil engineer Reidar Frank Agdestein and secretary Unni Jørgensen. Maternal grandfather was Reidar Jørgensen, a runner and botanist, suggesting an athletic and intellectual family background.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a civil engineer and mother a secretary; maternal grandfather was a runner and botanist, providing an athletic-intellectual family environment but not direct chess domain expertise.
primary_early_advantage_tags: prodigy chess talent,norwegian chess ecosystem,dual sport career,early grandmaster
evidence_summary: Agdestein demonstrated exceptional cognitive ability by becoming Norwegian champion at 15 and Grandmaster at 18, a rare feat requiring thousands of hours of study and play from a very young age. Norway's growing chess culture, later supercharged by Magnus Carlsen (whom Agdestein coached), provided a supportive ecosystem. His dual career as a professional footballer alongside elite chess demonstrated extraordinary physical and mental capacity. The combination of prodigy-level chess talent and athletic ability is exceptionally rare.
starting_point: Born in Asker, Norway to a civil engineer father and secretary mother; maternal grandfather was a runner and botanist, suggesting a family environment valuing both intellectual and athletic pursuits.
current_position: Chess grandmaster, coach at Norges Toppidrettsgymnas sports academy, and author; former coach of world champion Magnus Carlsen; continues to compete and won his ninth Norwegian Championship in 2023 at age 56.

trajectory.event: Won his first Norwegian Chess Championship, becoming the youngest champion ever, and won an individual gold medal at his first Chess Olympiad appearance.
Awarded the International Master title.
Awarded the Grandmaster title, one of the youngest in the world at the time.
Finished second at the World Junior Chess Championship behind Walter Arencibia, ahead of Viswanathan Anand.
Made his debut for the Norway national football team, combining elite chess with professional football.
Published 'Wonderboy,' a book about coaching Magnus Carlsen to become the youngest chess grandmaster in the world.
Won his ninth Norwegian Chess Championship, breaking the record for the oldest champion.
